Chapter 8 • Integrals

8.1 Volume Forms and Orientation

  • Given a smooth manifold \((\mathcal{M}, \mathcal{O}, \mathcal{A})_d\), a volume form is a \((0,d)\)-tensor field \begin{align*} \Omega : \underbrace{\Gamma T\mathcal{M} \times \dots \times \Gamma T\mathcal{M}}_{d\text{-times}} &\xlongrightarrow{\substack{\sim \\ \dots \\ \sim}} C^\infty(\mathcal{M}) \\ \big( \mathcal{X}_{(1)}, \dots, \mathcal{X}_{(d)} \big) &\longmapsto \Omega\big( \mathcal{X}_{(1)}, \dots, \mathcal{X}_{(d)} \big), \end{align*} satisfying:

    1. Non-vanishing: \(\Omega_p \neq 0\) for all \(p \in \mathcal{M}\);

    2. Total antisymmetry: exchanging any two arguments flips the sign, \[ \Omega\big( \dots, \underbrace{\mathcal{X}_{(a)}}_{a\text{-th}}, \dots, \underbrace{\mathcal{X}_{(b)}}_{b\text{-th}}, \dots \big) = - \Omega\big( \dots, \underbrace{\mathcal{X}_{(b)}}_{a\text{-th}}, \dots, \underbrace{\mathcal{X}_{(a)}}_{b\text{-th}}, \dots \big) \qquad \forall \, a \neq b \in \{1, \dots, d\} . \]

  • The \(d\)-dimensional Levi-Civita symbol is the array \(\varepsilon_{i_1 \dots i_d} = \varepsilon^{i_1 \dots i_d}\), \(i_1, \dots, i_d \in \{1, \dots, d\}\), fixed by \(\varepsilon_{1 \dots d} = 1\) and total antisymmetry, \(\varepsilon_{\dots i_a \dots i_b \dots} = - \varepsilon_{\dots i_b \dots i_a \dots}\)3. It vanishes if two indices coincide (exchanging them gives \(\varepsilon = -\varepsilon\)), and otherwise equals the sign of the permutation \((i_1, \dots, i_d)\) of \((1, \dots, d)\). For a totally antisymmetric array \(T_{i_1 \dots i_d}\) and a matrix \(T^i_j\) (we’ll employ these properties afterwards)4: \[ \underbrace{T_{i_1 \dots i_d} = \varepsilon_{i_1 \dots i_d} \, T_{1 \dots d}}_{\text{(a)}}, \qquad \underbrace{\det \big( T^i_j \big) = \varepsilon_{i_1 \dots i_d} \, T^{i_1}_1 \cdots T^{i_d}_d}_{\text{(b)}}, \qquad \underbrace{\varepsilon_{i_1 \dots i_d} \, T^{i_1}_{j_1} \cdots T^{i_d}_{j_d} = \det \big( T^i_j \big) \, \varepsilon_{j_1 \dots j_d}}_{\text{(c)}} . \]

  • In a chart \((\mathcal{U}, \mathscr{X})\), the components of a volume form, \((\Omega_\mathscr{X})_{i_1 \dots i_d} \coloneqq \Omega\big( \partial x_{i_1}, \dots, \partial x_{i_d} \big) \in C^\infty(\mathcal{U})\), form a totally antisymmetric array: \[ (\Omega_\mathscr{X})_{i_1 \dots i_d} = \varepsilon_{i_1 \dots i_d} \, \omega_\mathscr{X} , \qquad \omega_\mathscr{X} \coloneqq (\Omega_\mathscr{X})_{1 \dots d} = \Omega\big( \partial x_1, \dots, \partial x_d \big) \in C^\infty(\mathcal{U}) . \] The function \(\omega_\mathscr{X}\) is the scalar density of \(\Omega\) w.r.t. \((\mathcal{U}, \mathscr{X})\). As every component is \(\pm \omega_\mathscr{X}\) or \(0\), the non-vanishing condition reads \(\omega_\mathscr{X}(p) \neq 0\, \forall p \in \mathcal{U}\). Under a change of chart, on \(\mathcal{U} \cap \mathcal{V}\), \begin{align} \omega_\mathscr{Y} &\coloneqq \Omega\big( \partial y_1, \dots, \partial y_d \big) = \frac{\partial \mathscr{X}^{i_1}}{\partial \mathscr{Y}^1} \cdots \frac{\partial \mathscr{X}^{i_d}}{\partial \mathscr{Y}^d} \; \Omega\big( \partial x_{i_1}, \dots, \partial x_{i_d} \big) = \tag{8.1}\\ &= \frac{\partial \mathscr{X}^{i_1}}{\partial \mathscr{Y}^1} \cdots \frac{\partial \mathscr{X}^{i_d}}{\partial \mathscr{Y}^d} \; (\Omega_\mathscr{X})_{i_1 \dots i_d} \, = \frac{\partial \mathscr{X}^{i_1}}{\partial \mathscr{Y}^1} \cdots \frac{\partial \mathscr{X}^{i_d}}{\partial \mathscr{Y}^d} \, \varepsilon_{i_1 \dots i_d} \, \omega_\mathscr{X} \overset{(c)}{=} \det \left( \frac{\partial \mathscr{X}^i}{\partial \mathscr{Y}^j} \right) \omega_\mathscr{X}. \tag{8.2} \end{align} Therefore, under a change of basis, the scalar density \(\omega_\mathscr{X}\) picks up a Jacobian determinant term.5 In particular, \(\omega_\mathscr{X}\) is not a scalar field on \(\mathcal{M}\): its values at a point depend on the chart.

  • Let \((\mathcal{M}, \mathcal{O}, \mathcal{A})_d\) be a smooth manifold, with \(\mathcal{A}\) its maximal atlas. An atlas \(\mathcal{A}^\uparrow \subseteq \mathcal{A}\), i.e. a set of charts whose domains cover \(\mathcal{M}\), is an oriented atlas if all its Jacobian determinants are positive, \[ \det \left( \frac{\partial \mathscr{Y}^i}{\partial \mathscr{X}^j} \right)(p) > 0 \qquad \forall \, p \in \mathcal{U} \cap \mathcal{V}, \quad \forall \, (\mathcal{U}, \mathscr{X}), (\mathcal{V}, \mathscr{Y}) \in \mathcal{A}^\uparrow . \] The condition is symmetric in the two charts, since the two Jacobians are inverse matrices: \[ \det \left( \frac{\partial \mathscr{X}^i}{\partial \mathscr{Y}^j} \right) \, \det \left( \frac{\partial \mathscr{Y}^j}{\partial \mathscr{X}^k} \right) = \det \left( \frac{\partial \mathscr{X}^i}{\partial \mathscr{Y}^j} \frac{\partial \mathscr{Y}^j}{\partial \mathscr{X}^k} \right) = \det \big( \delta^i_k \big) = 1 . \] A smooth manifold is orientable if it admits an oriented atlas6, and the triple \((\mathcal{M}, \mathcal{O}, \mathcal{A}^\uparrow)\) is then an oriented manifold.

3

\(\varepsilon\) is a symbol, the same array in every chart, not the components of a tensor field. Its upper and lower versions have the same entries; the index position only allows them to enter the summation convention.

4

(a) As for \(\varepsilon\), \(T\) vanishes on repeated indices, and each exchange of two indices flips its sign. (b) \(\det \big( T^i_j \big) = \sum_\sigma \operatorname{sgn}(\sigma) \, T^{\sigma(1)}_1 \cdots T^{\sigma(d)}_d\), the terms with repeated indices dropping out of the sum over \(i_1, \dots, i_d\). (c) Relabelling \(i_a \leftrightarrow i_b\) shows that the left-hand side is totally antisymmetric in \(j_1, \dots, j_d\); by (a) it equals \(\varepsilon_{j_1 \dots j_d}\) times its value at \((1, \dots, d)\), which is \(\det \big( T^i_j \big)\) by (b).

5

Quantities that pick up a power \(\det\big( \partial \mathscr{X}^i / \partial \mathscr{Y}^j \big)^w\) under a change of chart are often called densities of weight \(w\). Defining what a density is, rather than how it transforms, requires intoducing the frame bundle of \(\mathcal{M}\) and the density bundles associated with it. For this chapter the transformation law is all that is needed, and \(\omega_\mathscr{X}\) can be viewed simply as function on \(\mathcal{U}\) attached to each chart.

6

Orientability is a global property: every chart domain, equipped with its single chart, is trivially oriented. The standard example of a non-orientable manifold is the Möbius strip.
